final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Latency-only incident with no errors and no restarts: all boutique pods 2/2 Running with RESTARTS=0, GetErrorLogs(cartservice/frontend)='No error logs found', events all Normal, and CheckServiceConnectivity(cartservice:7070)='Connection Succeeded' (reachable but slow). Alerts show a wave of p95 degradation across several services at once: cartservice 4.74->37.82ms (+697%), frontend 31.63->65.66ms (+108%), checkoutservice 28.86->76.12ms (+164%), plus redis-cart CPU/CFS throttle. Wide pods listing places cartservice, frontend and redis-cart on worker-01; checkoutservice (worker-02) is only a caller of worker-01-hosted cartservice/currencyservice, so its delay propagates across the call edge. Every service that runs only on worker-02 (adservice, emailservice, paymentservice, recommendationservice, shippingservice) is unaffected, giving a clean node-vs-node control. Nodes listing wide plus DescribeResource(node) on master/worker-01/worker-02/worker-03 and GetClusterConfiguration show all nodes Ready with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure, Taints=<none>, 8 allocatable CPUs and no NetworkUnavailable, and no prominent packet-retransmission value on any node; by the matched L3 rule (no retransmission peak -> delay class, node = placement pick) the case is a network delay on worker-01. Closing on the node surface, CheckNodeServiceStatus(worker-01, kube-proxy)=active (running) rules out runtime/service unavailability. First observation != expectation: several co-located services on worker-01 degrade while identically configured services on worker-02 do not -> breakpoint is worker-01's network plane, not any single pod's code.
